text: Found it: `Interval.fromISO` in src/interval.js calls `DateTime.fromISO` directly, so when `Settings.throwOnInvalid` is true the DateTime parse throws `InvalidDateTimeError` (and the `<start>/<duration>` / `<duration>/<end>` forms break) instead of falling through to `Interval.invalid`. Fixing it now (wrap the DateTime parses in try/catch and branch on validity flags). ETA ~5 min.

Found it: `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js converts years 0–99 by computing `Date.UTC(year, ...)` (which JS treats as 19xx) and then subtracting 1900 from the resulting year. When the day overflows into the next year, the rollover is computed with year 2000 (a leap year) instead of year 100 (not a leap year), so e.g. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 })` yields 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. Fix: re-specify month/day via `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` so the rollover uses the real year. ETA ~6 min.

Found it: the `isInDST` getter in src/datetime.js compares `this.offset` against `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset` and `this.set({ month: 5 }).offset`. `set({month: 1})` keeps the current day, so for a DateTime already in January it returns the same instant and the comparison is degenerate — e.g. `DateTime.fromISO("1974-02-15", {zone: "America/New_York"})` (offset -240, in DST) wrongly reports false. Fix: compare against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` (Jan 1 is standard time). ETA ~6 min.

Found it: in src/duration.js the `casualMatrix` `quarters` row is missing the `seconds` conversion factor (every other row lists all lower-order units, and the longterm/accurate matrix does have it). So `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 30}).normalize()` yields NaN, and converting between quarters and seconds breaks. Fix: add `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to that row. ETA ~7 min.

Found it: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js pads by prepending zeros and slicing the last n chars, which destroys the minus sign — `padStart(-50, 4)` gives "0-50". Since `toISODate()` uses `yyyy` → `padStart(year, 4)`, negative years come out as "0-50-05-25" instead of "-0050-05-25". Fix: handle the sign separately (pad the absolute value, re-attach "-"). ETA ~8 min.

Found it: `FixedOffsetZone` in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js hard-codes `get isValid() { return true; }`, so a zone built from a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` or `FixedOffsetZone.instance(NaN)`) claims to be valid and DateTimes in it are considered valid too. Fix: `return isNumber(this.fixed);` (importing `isNumber` from impl/util.js). ETA ~8 min.

Fixed and verified. `Interval.fromISO` now wraps its `DateTime.fromISO` and `Duration.fromISO` calls in try/catch, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` valid `<start>/<end>`, `<start>/<duration>` and `<duration>/<end>` inputs still parse and unparsable input throws an InvalidIntervalError (previously InvalidDateTimeError/InvalidDurationError). Full suite: same 2 pre-existing failures as before my change (French FFF/FFFF in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js), test/interval all green.

Fixed and verified. `objToLocalTS` now re-applies month/day via `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` instead of subtracting 1900 from the rolled-over year, so day rollovers out of year 99 use year 100's real calendar: 0099-12-31 + 61 days → 0100-03-02 (was 0100-03-01), +59 → 0100-02-28, +91 → 0100-04-01, and 0100-01-02 − 2 days → 0099-12-31. Matches plain JS Date arithmetic; no test regressions.

Fixed and verified. `isInDST` now compares against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` (Jan 1 is standard time) instead of `this.set({ month: 1 })`, which for a January DateTime returned the same instant and made the comparison degenerate. 1974 US year-round DST now reports correctly (1974-01-10, 1974-02-15, 1974-10-20 → true; 1974-11-15, 1975-02-15 → false), southern-hemisphere and normal cases unchanged, test/datetime/zone.test.js fully green.

Fixed and verified. The conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing two entries: `seconds` in the casual `quarters` row and `quarters: 4` in the `years` row of BOTH matrices. So `{quarters: 1, seconds: 30}.normalize()` and `{years: 1, quarters: 1}.normalize()` returned NaN, and years↔quarters / quarters↔seconds conversions were NaN. An exhaustive check of all 36 ordered unit pairs × {casual, longterm} now passes 72/72. No test regressions.

Fixed and verified. `padStart` no longer slices the sign off: it pads the absolute value and re-attaches "-", so `toISODate()`/`toISO()`/`toFormat("yyyy")` pad negative years correctly (-50 → "-0050-05-25", -5 → "-0005-05-25", -500 → "-0500-05-25"), while +118040, -118040, 1982 and year 3 are unchanged. No test regressions.

Fixed and verified. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` now returns `isNumber(this.fixed)` instead of hard-coded `true`, so a zone built with a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")`, `FixedOffsetZone.instance(null)`) is invalid, and a DateTime placed in such a zone is invalid with reason "unsupported zone". Valid zones (UTC, UTC±N, parseSpecifier, "UTC+3"/"UTC-8" strings) are unaffected; test/zones, test/info and test/datetime/zone.test.js all green.
